resources.string: How the paranasal sinuses clear mucus
Two views locate the four sinus groups, then a simplified cutaway follows normal mucus clearance in one maxillary sinus. The layers, movements, and timing are not to scale.
The frontal sinuses sit above the eyes, the ethmoid air cells between them, and the maxillary sinuses beneath them. The side view shows the sphenoid sinuses deep behind the ethmoid cells.

In this front-facing slice, the natural opening is high on the wall nearest the nose, well above the sinus floor. With the head upright, mucus has to move up to reach it. Gravity alone cannot do that.
Mucus from secretory cells joins a thin film over the sinus lining. Tiny, hairlike cilia on neighboring cells beat just beneath that film.
Coordinated cilia move the mucus film along the lining, up the walls toward the natural opening. The cutaway highlights one of those surface routes.
Mucus passes through the natural opening and a short channel into the middle meatus, a passage under the middle nasal turbinate. Nasal cilia carry it onward along the lining.
